text.about:
Jessica Zander is a garden coach and content creator based in the Boston area, doing virtual consultations all over the country and Canada.
She has been gardening for over 30 years and she started You Can Do It Gardening in 2022, to help people feel more confident about doing it themselves. With a passion for helping others discover the joy of gardening, she teaches skills, provides guidance and suggestions about plants and design, and works collaboratively and efficiently with clients to help them make small and large improvements in their outdoor spaces. 
After a 30-year career in nonprofit finance and operations she left the field in June of 2023 in response to the explosive demand for coaching services. Since the launch of the business, Jess has met with over 2,000 clients and heard from countless others who have expressed frustration, confusion, and surprise about the some of the challenges of gardening. It is one of her greatest joys to help people save money and feel more confident. She is direct and to the point, like Mary Poppins, but for your garden.   
In addition to her own gardening experience she has certificates from the UMASS Green School and NAISMA, in Terrestrial Invasive Plant Management.
Social media @youcandoitgardening

befores-and-afters.description: This was just mulch and pine needles. Free plants from a Facebook group helped this client with a weekend makeover.
We expanded the bed by moving one of the existing shrubs, dividing existing hostas, buying one new shrub and mulch. This cost about $70.

Planting young plants is an economical way to approach gardening, but you have to be patient. This is a gradual transformation over a few years. More plants were added and given a chance to grow in. 2012 to 2025.
This area was dark and overgrown. Now it features a more defined space, after major pruning and clearing, and adding a greater variety of plants.

This area had too many curves for such a small space, and the tree hydrangeas were too close to the neighboring plants on the other side of the fence. The hydrangeas were moved and a more proportional shape was created.
My mother was very skeptical about the potential for this area and she was an amazing gardener; however, any area can be transformed if you know what can be done to improve it.

text.personal-statement: At times, life can be very challenging and difficult.  Happiness, peace of mind and intimacy may be what you want but seem impossible to achieve. I am committed to working with you to help you understand why you feel the way you do and what you can do to feel better.  As a holistic psychotherapist, my goal is to understand you as whole person - mind, body and spirit.   I provide a supportive and transformational therapeutic experience where you can learn to feel more joy and connection with yourself and others.  I will help you heal from emotional, physical, and spiritual pain so that you may experience a more fulfilling and meaningful life.  If you are looking for extra support and guidance through a challenging situation or want to improve your overall quality of life, I look forward to working with you to achieve your goals.
text.psychotherapy-body-text:
Nicole Levin is a licensed clinical social worker, psychotherapist, educator, and movement facilitator dedicated to supporting healing, growth, and authentic self-expression. She earned her Master of Social Work degree from the University of Pennsylvania in 1997 and has spent nearly three decades helping individuals and groups deepen awareness, resilience, and wellbeing.
In her private psychotherapy practice, Nicole works with adults experiencing anxiety, depression, trauma, relationship challenges, and life transitions. Her approach is grounded in Gestalt therapy and emphasizes present-moment awareness, emotional integration, and meaningful connection.
Nicole serves on the faculty of the Pennsylvania Gestalt Center, where she teaches in the professional training program, leads workshops, and facilitates experiential group processes. She is passionate about creating spaces where people can explore themselves more fully through dialogue, relationship, and direct experience.
As a Group Motion Dance Facilitator, Nicole leads improvisational movement experiences that integrate mind, body, and spirit, inviting participants to access creativity, embodiment, and connection through movement. She is also a yoga and holistic movement teacher who has taught at nonprofit organizations, health centers, and the Kripalu Center for Yoga & Health.
Nicole leads day-long workshops and weekend retreats that weave together breath, movement, self-exploration, and community. Her work offers opportunities for participants to reconnect with themselves, expand their awareness, and cultivate greater vitality, presence, and personal growth.

text.main-header: Transform Your Tomorrow: Executive Function Coaching for Teens and Young Adults
text.main-subtitle:
Nothing should stand in the way of a student's ability to realize their full potential. As an Executive Function Coach, I combine the educational elements of academic tutoring with the benefits of ADHD coaching. By tailoring my approach to meet each student’s unique needs, I aim to help individuals maximize their strengths while targeting specific areas that need support.
Together, we will work on improving organizational and time management skills in a judgment-free environment, ensuring that each student has the necessary tools to excel in the academic world and beyond.
text.about-blurb:
Hi, I'm Rachel Dayanim and I'm excited to partner with you on your coaching journey. As an Executive Function Coach and Learning Specialist, I have worked for over twenty years supporting students of all ages both in schools and through my private practice. I also served as the Director of Student Support at an independent school and I am currently an instructional coach for ADAC and a Collegiate Learning Specialist at Focus Collegiate, supporting college students as they navigate their higher education experience.
Many of my clients have neurodiverse profiles (Autism, ADHD, Asperger's and other learning differences), and I partner with them to recognize their strengths and abilities, create and implement tools to support their success and help them achieve their personal goals.
I earned a Master of Arts in Special Education from Columbia University, with a specialty in Learning Disabilities and an ADHD Coaching Certification from JST Coaching. Additionally, I graduated with a Bachelor of Arts degree in Early Childhood and Elementary Education from Yeshiva University.

text.our-methods:
At Beyond the Bell Education Center, we take pride in creating a nurturing environment where students thrive. Our welcoming staff and sensory-friendly space, along with our joyful approach to learning, foster an atmosphere that supports improved student success in social skills, executive functioning, and academics.
We firmly believe that the key to quality teaching lies in building strong connections. Throughout your child's journey with us, we prioritize understanding their unique strengths, interests, goals, and challenges. Armed with this knowledge, we tailor individual or small group educational lessons and activities that are both creative and fun, ultimately leading to enhanced student success in social skills, executive functioning, and academics.
Our ultimate goal is to empower every student, ensuring they experience growth in their skills while feeling valued, appreciated, and included in our community. Join us at Beyond the Bell for a fulfilling and enriching educational experience!

text.meet-the-director:
Nancy Mager has always loved kids, and her passion is understanding each child’s motivation, strengths and struggles. Nancy has a Bachelor's degree in psychology from Boston University and a Master’s degree in special education from Simmons College. She’s spent the last 25 years working in the field of special education, with a strong interest in autism spectrum disorders and mental health. Professionally, Nancy has worked as a classroom teacher, behavioral and educational consultant, student advocate, adjunct college instructor, and most recently as the Director of Education for a non-profit.
Nancy has been trained extensively in the practices and philosophy of Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA), Social Thinking©, the Picture Exchange Communication System© (PECS), multiple assistive technology programs, TEACCH Autism (University of North Carolina), STARS Autism (Naperville, IL), Moving Traditions; It’s a Girls Thing©, and crisis prevention.

text.social-skills:
Our Social Skills groups are more like a playdate with a coach than a class in social rules and expectations. While many children can tell you what the social expectations are in a given situation, they may not be able to access those skills to demonstrate them when that situation occurs. This is why teaching social skills in a more natural setting is important.
Our staff begins by building relationships with each child in order to understand their unique perspective and what strengths and skills they bring to BTB. We then try to foster the development of friendships with unique shared experiences. When tricky situations arise, staff are fully involved in the activities and can step in to help students work through problems in the moment.
The structure of our groups is predictable, yet the activities are always changing based upon student requests, curiosities and interests.
text.social-skills-details-header: More About Social Skills at Beyond The Bell
text.social-skills-details:
Groups of 2-8 students meet weekly during the school year for 60-90 minutes.
Group Sessions include the following structure:
-Free and Me Time (transition time when students can explore BTB or just relax as they transition between environments)
-Group Meeting (when the whole group comes together for information sharing, community building, group games or group activities)
-Interest-based activity (rotating high interest activities based on group dynamic and preferences)
text.1-on-1-tutoring:
Beyond The Bell respects all children for their unique learning profiles. We believe that all children will thrive when provided with appropriate accommodations, positive behavioral supports and skilled, engaging educators.
Beyond The Bell provides carefully organized, one-hour tutoring sessions in all areas of academics. Students engaging with BTB tutoring services receive the necessary assistance in subjects like math, reading, science, and social studies.
For struggling and emerging readers we offer 1:1 support using the Wilson Reading System©, a multi-sensory approach to literacy instruction. We offer instruction with a certified Wilson reading specialist to students whose basic literacy skills are below that of their peers, despite conventional interventions.

Whether you are planning a Wedding, Bar/Bat Mitzvah, Organizational Gala or Banquet, Community Concert, or any special celebration, we can help make it memorable and enjoyable.
Ensembles are configured to meet your specific needs. We listen to your plans, offer some possible approaches to achieve your ideal result, and then carefully prepare and configure our services accordingly.

You may be relieved to know that the person with whom you are discussing your plans will be either facilitating your event or working closely with whomever is implementing these plans so the chance for confusion and mistakes are minimized. Imagine some of your favorite movies. The music probably played an important part in the overall experience. Music can help set the tone and tell a meaningful story. We can make it happen.
